elements.name: User

elements.name: JpaUtil
elements.role: Manages EntityManagerFactory lifecycle and database connections.

elements.name: PersistenceService
elements.role: Owns and encapsulates the persistence layer operations using JPA and JpaUtil.

elements.name: ReportService
elements.role: Handles business logic and persistence coordination for reports, notes, and notifications.

elements.name: UserService
elements.role: Handles business logic and persistence coordination for users and credentials.

notes: RI-1: PersistenceService encapsulates the database access, while ReportService and UserService handle the business logic.
RI-2: Database layer classes are grouped in Database package; entities and service layers are grouped in Entity package.
RI-3: PersistenceService is the primary module owning the persistence layer.

AQ1: Persistent entities include User (with subclasses Citizen and MunicipalOperator), Report, Credentials, Location, ReportCategory, ReportStatus, InternalNote, and Notification. Report has relationships to Citizen, MunicipalOperator, InternalNote, and StatusUpdate.
AQ2: PersistenceService and JpaUtil own and encapsulate the persistence layer for municipal reports.
AQ3: Business logic components (ReportService, UserService) instantiate and call PersistenceService methods (save, update, findById, findByFields) to interact with the database.
AQ4: JPA annotations (@Entity, @Table, @Id, @GeneratedValue, @ManyToOne, @OneToMany, @Embeddable) implement data entities and manage their lifecycle.

AQ5: State updates are initiated through ReportService.updateReportStatus, calling report.updateStatus() which executes transitions via ReportStatus implementations, registers a StatusUpdate, and persists changes via PersistenceService.update(report).
